model.name: Risk / Opportunity
model.purpose: Govern the identified risk or opportunity as a persistent, identified record of an uncertain future event or condition whose occurrence would affect stated objectives, carrying its articulation, classification, likelihood and consequence estimates, evaluation against criteria, response decision, lifecycle state, ownership and provenance.
model.scope_statement: This model covers the registered uncertainty item itself: how it is defined, identified, articulated as a source-event-consequence scenario, classified against versioned schemes, estimated for likelihood and consequence over a declared horizon, evaluated against risk criteria and an appetite or tolerance reference, assigned a response option, linked by reference to treatment actions and controls, moved through lifecycle states to realisation or closure, owned, provenanced, aggregated into registers and snapshots, validated, protected and projected into external schemas. It is deliberately symmetric: adverse (threat) and beneficial (opportunity) items share one identity, criteria and lifecycle machinery, with valence recorded as a coded field. It does not perform, execute or enforce anything: treatment execution, control assurance, incident handling, objective setting, decision authority, evidence capture, audit trails and retention execution belong to referenced sibling models or the adopting Dimension. The model is storage- and interface-neutral; register tables, documents, graphs and message payloads are projections of the same semantics.
in_scope: The identified risk or opportunity item as a governed record, threat-side and opportunity-side under one identity
Scenario articulation: risk source or cause, uncertain event, consequence, and the exposed object
Boundary tests separating an item from an issue, incident, hazard, control deficiency or assumption
Classification against versioned schemes plus valence and inherent/current/residual/target framing
Likelihood and consequence estimates with declared scales, units, horizon and conditionality
Level of risk, combination rule, aggregation limits, evaluation outcome and priority candidate
Assessment technique, assumptions, inputs, confidence and references to supporting evidence
Response option selection and referenced treatment actions, controls and mitigating factors
Lifecycle states, review cadence and triggers, realisation hand-off and closure outcomes
Ownership, acceptance and escalation authority references, and assertion provenance
Register membership, point-in-time snapshots and reporting extracts as artifacts
Validation rules, sensitivity classification, and alignment or crosswalk records with recorded conflicts
out_of_scope: Execution, scheduling and change control of treatment actions and projects
Control design, testing, effectiveness assurance and audit opinions
Incident, issue and loss-event handling, investigation and post-event response
Objective, strategy and target setting, and performance measurement of objectives
Threat intelligence, hazard catalogues and vulnerability management
Capture and lifecycle of observations and evidence records, including chain of custody
Setting enterprise risk appetite and tolerance statements (referenced, not authored here)
Delegated authority schemes, approval workflow engines and runtime policy evaluation or enforcement
Platform audit-trail creation and retention or erasure execution, including legal hold mechanics
AI-system conformity assessment, high-risk classification and regulatory enforcement
Insurance contracts, actuarial pricing, risk transfer instruments and regulatory capital calculation
Dashboards, business intelligence and board reporting cadence built on register extracts

boundary_notes.distinction: An item ceases to be a risk when the uncertain event occurs. The materialised event, its measured losses and its response are owned by the incident or loss-event model; this model retains only the realisation flag, the event time and a reference.
Threats and hazards are reusable catalogue entries referenced by identifier, mirroring the OSCAL threat-id pattern. This model neither maintains threat taxonomies nor produces intelligence.
Controls and mitigating factors are referenced with an effectiveness input recorded as evidence. Control design, testing and assurance opinions remain in the control model.

Supporting observations are referenced, following the OSCAL related-observations pattern. Evidence capture, custody and lifecycle are not owned here; only reference, digest and relevance note are held.

Risk is defined as an effect of uncertainty on objectives, so objectives are referenced, never authored here. Objective definition, targets and performance reporting stay with the parent action or objective model.

An AI governance assessment references items here as risk evidence. The AI-specific risk-management-system obligation, residual-risk acceptability determination, conformity assessment and enforcement remain with that model and the competent authority.

Acceptance, escalation and closure decisions are carried as decision references with the authority level asserted at the time. Delegation schemes, approval workflow and enforcement are not modelled here.
Register snapshots and reporting extracts are defined as immutable artifacts of this model; dashboards, roll-up analytics and reporting cadence belong to the adopting Dimension.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Insurance, risk transfer and capital models
boundary_notes.distinction: Only the sharing or transfer response option and its contract reference are recorded. Pricing, capital requirement calculation and loss-distribution modelling for capital are excluded.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Platform audit trail and access enforcement
boundary_notes.distinction: This model states what must be auditable and what sensitivity applies, but does not create, hold or enforce audit records or access decisions.

findings.name: Definitional frame and objective linkage
findings.description: An item is a recorded assertion that an uncertain event or condition, if it occurs, would have an effect on stated objectives; the governing definition (neutral effect-on-objectives versus adverse likelihood-and-impact) must be declared because authoritative sources disagree.

data_elements.name: Definition scheme
data_elements.description: Coded declaration of the risk definition under which the item was recorded, with the standard reference it derives from.

data_elements.name: Affected objective reference
data_elements.description: Reference to one or more objectives in the owning objective or activity model that the uncertainty acts upon.

data_elements.name: Uncertainty basis
data_elements.description: Short statement of why occurrence is uncertain, used to distinguish an open item from a materialised condition.

findings.name: Scenario articulation: source, event, consequence
findings.description: The item is stated as a chain of risk source or cause, an uncertain event, and the consequence on the exposed object, at a granularity that keeps items separable and assessable.

data_elements.name: Risk source or cause
data_elements.description: The element which alone or in combination has the potential to give rise to the event, held as text plus optional reference to a threat or hazard catalogue entry.

data_elements.name: Uncertain event description
data_elements.description: Description of the occurrence or change of circumstances whose happening is uncertain.

data_elements.name: Consequence description
data_elements.description: Description of the outcome affecting objectives should the event occur.

data_elements.name: Exposed object reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the asset, process, service or population exposed to the consequence.

findings.name: Boundary against adjacent concepts
findings.description: Explicit tests separating an open risk or opportunity from an issue or incident, a threat or hazard, a control deficiency, an observation, and a planning assumption or dependency.

data_elements.name: Boundary test outcome
data_elements.description: Recorded result of the admissibility tests applied at registration, including which adjacent concept was ruled out.

data_elements.name: Related adjacent-concept reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a threat, control deficiency, observation, assumption or incident record that the item is related to but is not.

findings.name: Item identity, revision and continuity
findings.description: Identity of the item is stable and separate from the identity of any assessment revision; re-estimation creates a revision, while split, merge or withdrawal are explicit continuity events.

data_elements.name: Item identifier
data_elements.description: Primary identifier of the item, assigned per the identity priority rule and opaque within its namespace.

data_elements.name: Master-system record key
data_elements.description: Identifier held by the authoritative register system of record, where such a system exists.

data_elements.name: Alternate identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the same item in another register or schema, carried with its source namespace and never used as the primary key.

data_elements.name: Assessment revision identifier
data_elements.description: Monotonic revision identifier for the assessment state of the item, distinct from the item identity.

data_elements.name: Supersession reference
data_elements.description: Reference to items superseded, split from or merged into this item, with the continuity event type.

findings.name: Classification against versioned schemes
findings.description: Items are classified using one or more published schemes, each identified with a version; scheme boundaries are normative and category sets are not interchangeable between sectors.

data_elements.name: Category assignment
data_elements.description: Coded category with its scheme identifier, scheme version and assignment provenance.

data_elements.name: Classification scheme version
data_elements.description: Version of the scheme in force at the moment of assignment, retained even after the scheme is superseded.

findings.name: Valence and assessment framing
findings.description: Whether the item is adverse, beneficial or two-sided, and which framings (inherent, current, residual, target) the recorded estimates represent, since standards differ on both points.

data_elements.name: Valence
data_elements.description: Coded direction of the assessed effect: adverse, beneficial, or two-sided.

data_elements.name: Assessment framing
data_elements.description: Coded framing of a given estimate: inherent, current, residual or target, with the controls assumed in force.

findings.name: Register scope and context binding
findings.description: Each item is registered against a scope (organisational unit, portfolio, system or programme) and records the internal and external context assumed when it was scoped, which determines the applicable criteria set.

data_elements.name: Register scope
data_elements.description: Identifier of the register, unit or portfolio the item belongs to, which drives criteria applicability and escalation.

data_elements.name: Jurisdiction or location applicability
data_elements.description: Coded jurisdiction, site or territory for which the item and its estimates hold.

data_elements.name: Assumed context factor
data_elements.description: Recorded internal or external context factor or dependency assumed at scoping, with an optional reference to the source record.

findings.name: Time horizon, onset and assessment validity
findings.description: Likelihood is meaningless without a horizon: the model records the exposure window the estimate refers to, the expected speed of onset, and the date until which the assessment is treated as current.

data_elements.name: Assessment horizon
data_elements.description: Start and end of the exposure window over which likelihood and consequence are judged.

data_elements.name: Assessment valid-until
data_elements.description: Timestamp after which the current assessment is considered stale and must be re-reviewed.

data_elements.name: Speed of onset
data_elements.description: Estimated interval between event occurrence and consequence materialisation, with unit.

findings.name: Likelihood expression and scale binding
findings.description: Likelihood may be an ordinal band, a probability or a frequency; whichever is used, the scale definition, version, exposure window and any conditionality must be recorded with the value.

data_elements.name: Likelihood value
data_elements.description: The recorded likelihood expressed as a band label, probability or frequency, always paired with its representation code.

data_elements.name: Likelihood scale reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the scale definition that gives the value its meaning.

data_elements.name: Likelihood conditioning assumptions
data_elements.description: Events or controls assumed present or absent when the likelihood was judged.

findings.name: Consequence dimensions and magnitude
findings.description: Consequence is recorded per dimension (financial, safety, legal, service, environmental, reputational and others in force), with magnitude, unit or currency, valuation basis, case basis and who bears the effect.

data_elements.name: Consequence dimension
data_elements.description: Coded dimension along which a consequence is assessed.

data_elements.name: Consequence magnitude
data_elements.description: Magnitude per dimension with unit or currency code, valuation basis and reference date for monetary values.

data_elements.name: Case basis
data_elements.description: Whether the magnitude is expected, most likely or worst credible, so that values are not silently compared across bases.

data_elements.name: Affected party reference
data_elements.description: Reference to parties or populations bearing the consequence, including external bearers.

findings.name: Level of risk, priority and aggregation limits
findings.description: The level or exposure derives from a declared combination rule whose validity limits must be recorded, and aggregation or roll-up across items is permitted only under stated correlation and comparability conditions.

data_elements.name: Level of risk
data_elements.description: Derived level or exposure value with the identifier of the combination rule and framing that produced it.

data_elements.name: Priority
data_elements.description: Relative importance of the item within its register scope, recorded with the method used to derive it.

data_elements.name: Aggregation eligibility
data_elements.description: Flag and rationale stating whether the item's values may be aggregated with others, given scale and basis comparability.

findings.name: Risk criteria, appetite reference and evaluation outcome
findings.description: Evaluation compares the level against a versioned criteria set and a referenced appetite or tolerance statement, yielding an outcome and, where the item sits outside appetite, an escalation record; appetite is authored elsewhere and only referenced here.

data_elements.name: Criteria set reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the risk criteria set applied, including the scales and thresholds in force.

data_elements.name: Appetite or tolerance reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the externally authored appetite or tolerance statement, with its version and the term sense used.

data_elements.name: Evaluation outcome
data_elements.description: Coded result of comparing the level of risk against criteria and appetite, with evaluation timestamp.

findings.name: Assessment technique, inputs and assumptions
findings.description: The technique used to produce the estimate is identified with its assumptions, exclusions, data sources or expert inputs, so that the estimate is reproducible and its applicability can be challenged.

data_elements.name: Assessment technique reference
data_elements.description: Identifier of the technique applied, referencing an external technique catalogue rather than defining techniques locally.

data_elements.name: Assumption or exclusion
data_elements.description: Recorded assumption or exclusion conditioning the estimate, with an optional invalidation trigger.

data_elements.name: Estimate input reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a dataset, model run or expert elicitation used as input, with the time the input was obtained.

findings.name: Evidence references, confidence and knowledge limits
findings.description: The estimate carries a confidence statement on a declared scale, references to supporting observations or evidence held in their owning models, an account of knowledge limits and unquantified uncertainty, and a record of who challenged it.

data_elements.name: Confidence in estimate
data_elements.description: Declared confidence in the estimate with the scale that gives it meaning; ordinal confidence must not be read as probability.

data_elements.name: Supporting evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an observation or evidence record in its owning model, carried with a digest and relevance note only.

data_elements.name: Knowledge limitation
data_elements.description: Recorded gap, unquantified uncertainty or limit of available evidence affecting the estimate.

findings.name: Response option selection
findings.description: A response is selected from a governed option set that includes avoiding, taking or increasing the risk to pursue an opportunity, removing the source, changing the likelihood, changing the consequences, sharing and retaining, with rationale and, for retention, an authority reference.

data_elements.name: Response option
data_elements.description: Coded response option selected, from the governed option set in force for the register scope.

data_elements.name: Response rationale
data_elements.description: Recorded justification for the selected option, including proportionality or cost-benefit reasoning.

data_elements.name: Estimated response cost
data_elements.description: Estimated cost of the selected response with currency code and basis date.

findings.name: Treatment action and control references
findings.description: Planned treatment actions, existing controls and mitigating factors are carried as references with expected effect and deadline; execution, scheduling and control assurance stay with their owning models.

data_elements.name: Treatment action reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a planned or in-flight action in the owning action or plan model, with its owner and status source.

data_elements.name: Control or mitigating factor reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an existing control or a described mitigating factor relied upon in the current framing.

data_elements.name: Treatment deadline
data_elements.description: Timestamp by which the referenced treatment is required to be complete.

data_elements.name: Expected post-treatment level
data_elements.description: Target level of risk expected once the referenced treatment is effective, recorded in the target framing.

findings.name: Lifecycle states and permitted transitions
findings.description: The item moves through a declared state set with gated transitions and a mapping to external status vocabularies, which are threat-oriented and therefore only partially expressive for opportunities.

data_elements.name: Lifecycle state
data_elements.description: Current coded state of the item within the declared state set.

data_elements.name: State effective time
data_elements.description: Time from which the current state applies, recorded separately from the time the state change was written.

data_elements.name: External status code
data_elements.description: Status value projected into an external vocabulary for exchange, with the target schema version.

findings.name: Monitoring, review cadence and indicators
findings.description: Items are reviewed on a cadence and on trigger events; each review appends an immutable log entry recording who reviewed, what changed, the trend, and linked early-warning indicators.

data_elements.name: Next review due
data_elements.description: Timestamp by which the next scheduled review must occur.

data_elements.name: Trend
data_elements.description: Coded direction of travel of the level of risk since the previous review.

data_elements.name: Early-warning indicator reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an indicator and its threshold in the owning measurement model, used as a review trigger.

findings.name: Realisation, benefit capture and closure
findings.description: When the uncertain event occurs the item is marked realised and handed off to the incident or loss-event model; opportunities record realised benefit; closure records a permitted reason with supporting evidence.

data_elements.name: Realisation status
data_elements.description: Whether the uncertain event has occurred, with the occurrence time and the detecting source.

data_elements.name: Materialised event reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the incident or loss-event record that took ownership once the event occurred.

data_elements.name: Closure reason
data_elements.description: Coded reason the item was closed, such as treated, realised and handed off, no longer applicable, or merged.

findings.name: Ownership and role separation
findings.description: A single accountable owner is recorded for the item alongside distinct assessor, action-owner and reviewer roles, each attributable to a party and to an assurance line.

data_elements.name: Accountable owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party accountable for the item, resolved in the party or organisation model.

data_elements.name: Role assignment
data_elements.description: Assignment of a party to a role on this item, with the role code, assurance line and effective period.

findings.name: Acceptance, escalation and authority references
findings.description: The model records which authority level was relied upon, the decision reference that authorises the current disposition and the escalation path when the level exceeds local authority, without owning delegation schemes or approval workflow.

data_elements.name: Relied-upon authority level
data_elements.description: Coded authority level asserted as sufficient for the current disposition at the time it was recorded.

data_elements.name: Authorising decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the decision record that authorises acceptance, escalation or closure, held in the decision model.

findings.name: Assertion provenance and time separation
findings.description: Every value is attributable to an agent and an activity, derived from identifiable prior records, with event time, observation time and record time held separately and never substituted for one another.

data_elements.name: Asserting agent
data_elements.description: Identifier of the agent responsible for the asserted value, aligned to the PROV agent notion.

data_elements.name: Observation time
data_elements.description: Time at which the estimate or evidence was obtained, distinct from the time the record was written.

data_elements.name: Record or ingestion time
data_elements.description: Time at which the value was written to the register or ingested from another system.

data_elements.name: Derived-from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the prior record or source from which the value was derived.

findings.name: Register membership, snapshots and extracts
findings.description: A register is a scoped repository accumulating item information over time; membership rules, immutable point-in-time snapshots and derived reporting extracts are defined here, while retention execution and reporting cadence are not.

data_elements.name: Register membership
data_elements.description: Membership of the item in one or more registers, with the criteria version that admitted it.

data_elements.name: Retention class
data_elements.description: Coded retention class applied to the item and its artifacts, referencing the governing records policy.

findings.name: Validation, completeness and staleness rules
findings.description: Records are checked for mandatory fields per lifecycle state, conformance of values to declared scales, duplicate or overlapping items, and stale assessments, producing a defect list rather than silently amending values.

data_elements.name: Validation status
data_elements.description: Result of the most recent validation pass over the record, with the ruleset version applied.

data_elements.name: Validation defect
data_elements.description: Individual defect found, with severity, affected field and whether it blocks state transition or exchange.

findings.name: Sensitivity classification and access constraints
findings.description: Items carry a sensitivity classification covering their statement, evidence references and owner identity, with audience rules, personal-data minimisation and an explicit treatment of aggregation sensitivity; enforcement belongs to the platform.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity classification
data_elements.description: Coded sensitivity of the item record, referencing the classification scheme in force.

data_elements.name: Personal data presence
data_elements.description: Whether the record contains personal or identifying data requiring minimisation and restricted handling.

data_elements.name: Audience release rule
data_elements.description: Rule stating which audience may receive which fields, used to derive redacted reporting extracts.

findings.name: External alignment, lossy projection and recorded conflicts
findings.description: Alignments to external vocabularies and schemas are declared as versioned mappings with known losses, and definitional conflicts between authorities are recorded rather than resolved by fiat; conformance is claimed only with evidence.

data_elements.name: Alignment target
data_elements.description: External schema, vocabulary or taxonomy this model maps to, with its version and mapping direction.

data_elements.name: Mapping loss note
data_elements.description: Recorded loss or approximation introduced by a specific projection, tied to the affected field.

data_elements.name: Definitional conflict record
data_elements.description: Recorded disagreement between authoritative definitions affecting interpretation, with citations and the local disambiguation applied.

functions.name: Register risk or opportunity item
functions.description: Admit a new item to a register scope with its statement, valence, definition scheme, objective reference and provenance, minting identity under the identity priority rule.

functions.name: Classify item against a scheme
functions.description: Assign coded categories from one or more published, versioned classification schemes and retain superseded assignments.

functions.name: Estimate likelihood and consequence
functions.description: Produce a new assessment revision holding likelihood and consequence values with their scales, horizon, technique, assumptions, evidence references and confidence.

functions.name: Evaluate against criteria and appetite
functions.description: Derive the level of risk from the current revision using the declared combination rule and compare it with criteria thresholds and the referenced appetite or tolerance statement.

functions.name: Record response decision
functions.description: Record the response option selected from the governed option set together with its rationale, cost estimate and the authorising decision reference.

functions.name: Bind treatment and control references
functions.description: Attach references to planned actions, existing controls and mitigating factors, with expected post-treatment effect and deadline.

functions.name: Transition lifecycle state
functions.description: Move an item to a permitted target state, recording the trigger, effective time and record time, and appending the transition to the review log.

functions.name: Record review outcome
functions.description: Append an immutable review log entry capturing reviewer, changes, trend and next review date, following a scheduled cadence or a trigger event.

functions.name: Hand off realised item
functions.description: Mark the item realised when the uncertain event occurs, record the occurrence time and the receiving incident, loss-event or benefit record, and move the item to closure.

functions.name: Compile register view or snapshot
functions.description: Produce a register view for a scope and as-of time, or an immutable snapshot and audience-specific reporting extract derived from it.

functions.name: Validate item or register record
functions.description: Apply the published validation ruleset to check mandatory fields, scale conformance, duplicates and staleness, and emit a defect list.

functions.name: Emit alignment projection
functions.description: Project selected items into an external schema or vocabulary using a published crosswalk and record the losses incurred.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must be kept apart. The frozen registry value 'standalone-mm' with record_plane 'world-model' classifies how the registry record itself is carried in the registry plane — it says the model is a standalone meta-model record rather than a contained fragment — and it is not a member of the subject-model enum, so it can never be the subject kind. On the subject axis the governed thing is a persistent, identified register item: it holds a stable identifier separate from its assessment revisions, moves through gated lifecycle states, carries a single accountable owner, survives re-estimation, split, merge, withdrawal and closure, and is referenced by WM-AI-008 as a durable target. That is 'entity'. 'event' is rejected because the uncertain event is the item's referent, not the record — the model explicitly loses custody at realisation and hands the materialised event to the incident or loss-event model, so typing it as an event would erase the entire pre-occurrence lifecycle that is the model's substance. 'aggregate' and 'registry' are rejected at entry level because the risk register, its snapshots and its reporting extracts are declared artifacts and derived projections of the item, and making the register the root would make membership changes rewrite item identity; whether the register deserves a separate registry-kind sibling is recorded as deferred, not resolved here. The aggregate root is therefore the individual risk or opportunity item, with assessment revisions, review log entries, treatment plans and closure records composed under its identity.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root: individual item versus the risk register
decisions.disposition: accepted — item is the root, register stays an artifact
decisions.rationale: Item identity is asserted to persist independently of register membership, and snapshots and extracts are derived, sequence-identified artifacts. Rooting the model on the register would make a membership or scope change mutate item identity and would contradict the identity-priority rule.

decisions.concept: Subject entry kind 'entity' versus frozen registry 'standalone-mm'
decisions.disposition: accepted as entity; registry value read as record-plane classifier only
decisions.rationale: The registry field classifies the record plane (a standalone meta-model record) and is absent from the subject-model enum. The provider's declared 'entity' is the defensible subject kind and no reclassification of the provider judgement is required, only an explicit two-axis note in the published draft.

decisions.concept: Alternative entry kind 'event'
decisions.disposition: rejected
decisions.rationale: The uncertain event is the referent of the record, not the record. The model surrenders the materialised event to the incident or loss-event model at realisation and keeps only a flag, an event time and a reference, so an event kind would discard the pre-occurrence lifecycle the model exists to govern.

decisions.concept: Alternative entry kinds 'aggregate' and 'registry'
decisions.disposition: rejected at entry level; register-as-sibling deferred
decisions.rationale: Register, snapshot and reporting extract are declared artifacts with their own serial identity rules, and f-register-aggregation owns membership rather than being owned by it. Whether a registry-kind sibling model should hold register scope, membership and retention is a real open question but does not change this entry's kind.

decisions.concept: Opportunity symmetry under one identity with valence as a coded field
decisions.disposition: accepted
decisions.rationale: Symmetry is claimed only at the conceptual level with ISO/TC 262 and Orange Book support, the falsification attempt for an opportunity-bearing external schema is recorded as failed, and every projection of a beneficial item is marked lossy. Splitting valence into two record types would duplicate identity, criteria and lifecycle machinery for no evidenced gain.

decisions.concept: Coverage checklist claim of 'fourteen composition links' under the relationships dimension
decisions.disposition: rejected as unsupported; downgrade relationships to partial pending delivery
decisions.rationale: The delivered payload contains no composition array, the frozen registry contains_ids is empty and the relationship contract carries a single WM-AI-008 REFERENCE edge. A covered status cannot rest on a structure that is not present in the evidence pack being audited.

decisions.concept: Dangling checklist identifier 'de-retention-class' in the retention and deletion note
decisions.disposition: rejected as a broken traceability pointer; must resolve to crud.delete and f-register-aggregation
decisions.rationale: No element with that identifier exists in the delivered bundle, layer, finding, artifact or function sets. Traceability citations in the coverage checklist must resolve to delivered identifiers or the checklist cannot be used as review evidence.

decisions.concept: Parent relation to WM-ACT-017 asserted in boundary notes and registry links
decisions.disposition: deferred pending relationship-contract ratification
decisions.rationale: The parent edge appears in registry parent_ids, in a boundary note and in the service-layer registry links, but the frozen relationship contract contains only the inbound WM-AI-008 REFERENCE. The draft may describe the intended parent plane but must not present the edge as ratified.

decisions.concept: Source support: ISO 31000 and ISO 31073 cited as primary tier-1 support without full-text retrieval
decisions.disposition: accepted with mandatory cited-but-unretrieved marking
decisions.rationale: The known_omissions honestly disclose that ISO texts are paywalled and that content is carried via ISO/TC 262 first-party material and public-authority restatements, but the source table still flags them primary_source true, which overstates evidentiary status for any downstream conformance claim.

decisions.concept: primary_source flag on aggregating NIST glossary entries and a TC 262 news item
decisions.disposition: reclassified as authoritative restatements rather than primary texts
decisions.rationale: SRC-008, SRC-009 and SRC-010 explicitly aggregate SP 800-30, SP 800-39, CNSSI 4009, OMB circulars and ISO Guide 73, and SRC-003 is a committee news item. They are legitimate support for the recorded definitional conflict but must not be published as primary sources of the definitions themselves.

decisions.concept: Access scopes declared as bundle, layer, finding and artifact
decisions.disposition: rejected as a research-plane leak; must map to item, register, revision and artifact scopes
decisions.rationale: Those four scopes describe this world-model document's own structure, not the governed subject records. A deny-by-default access rule that grants per register scope and sensitivity class needs subject-plane scopes, otherwise the interface specification cannot implement the stated field-group write separation.

decisions.concept: Retention, erasure and the tombstone contract
decisions.disposition: accepted
decisions.rationale: The model owns only retention class, disposition state, tombstone contract and policy reference, refuses hard deletion while any register, snapshot, extract or referencing model cites the item, preserves identifier, state, closure reason and provenance stubs under mandated erasure, and pushes scheduling, legal hold and physical erasure to the adopting Dimension. That is consistent with the non-enforcement policy and asserts no retention duration it cannot support.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity rules: serial naming, digest binding and timestamps demoted to metadata
decisions.disposition: accepted
decisions.rationale: Identity priority runs master-system key, governed IRI, minted UUID or ULID; no local identifier encodes a date, owner, category, severity or sensitivity; serial artifacts use namespace plus zero-padded monotonic sequence with tombstoned gaps; and a digest mismatch invalidates derived evaluations, views, projections and conformance claims rather than permitting repair.

decisions.concept: art-risk-statement-record carrying no identifier of its own beyond item identity and revision
decisions.disposition: accepted with a condition on the storage projection
decisions.rationale: A statement record with no independent key avoids a second identifier surface, but the integrity rule requires every artifact to carry a digest, asserting agent and record time, so the storage specification must state explicitly that the digest binds to item identifier plus revision or the artifact becomes unaddressable.
