model.name: Risk / Control
model.purpose: Provide an embeddable field group that binds one risk assessment context to a referenced risk, links it to referenced controls and their cited effectiveness determinations, and explains the residual position against referenced appetite or tolerance, without owning the risk entity, the control register or any treatment workflow.
model.scope_statement: WM-XCT-027 is a mixin: a reusable set of fields attached to a host record so that record can carry a defensible, revision-pinned risk assessment context. It owns the reference and binding fields (risk reference and exact revision, objective/asset/process/context anchors, source-event-consequence anchors), the pinned assessment frame (category and taxonomy pins, scope, exclusions, time horizon, criteria set, method and technique with versions, expression mode), the estimate slots (likelihood and consequence dimension declarations, inherent estimate with its exclusion statement, residual estimate with change explanation), the evidential basis (assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind, uncertainty and confidence qualification), the control-linkage references (relied-on control references and the effectiveness determinations cited for them), the governance stamps at assessment-context level (assessor, context owner, reviewer and acceptance-decision references, review-due timing), and the comparability surface (comparability verdicts, aggregation caveats, scenario dependence). It does not evaluate controls, does not run assessments, does not set or enforce appetite, does not grant acceptance or authorization, and does not define the internals of any pinned technique. Storage and interface are projections: the same field semantics must survive JSON, YAML, Markdown, HTML, Git, MCP and MongoDB representations.
in_scope: Reference to one risk or opportunity entity together with an exact revision or version pin of the assessed statement.
Anchor references the assessment is scoped against: objectives, assets, processes, organizational units, contextual conditions and applicable jurisdiction or site.
Causal-chain references: risk source or threat source, the event or event class quantified, and the consequences included or explicitly excluded.
Category values with an explicit taxonomy scheme identifier and version pin.
Assessment scope statement, exclusions, likelihood time horizon, as-of time of the assessed state, recording time and validity or review-due time.
Criteria set, assessment method and technique pins with their versions, plus the expression mode (qualitative, ordinal, semi-quantitative, quantitative, probabilistic, scenario-based).
Likelihood and consequence dimension declarations with units, scale references, distribution parameters and support for multi-dimensional impact.
Inherent (pre-control) estimate together with an explicit statement of what 'inherent' excluded in this context, or a documented ground for omitting it.
Assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind, analysis constraints and identification of critical assumptions.
Uncertainty representation, confidence or data-quality grading, unmeasurable aspects and precision caveats.
Control linkage: references to the controls relied on and to the effectiveness determinations cited for them, produced by the owning control assessment model.
Residual (post-control) estimate, the characterization state marking it as adjusted rather than initial, the changed-dimension set and the explanation of change.
References to the appetite or tolerance statement in force and the recorded outcome of comparing the residual estimate against it.
Assessment-context governance stamps: assessor, context owner, reviewer and acceptance-decision references, and review-due timing.
Comparability verdicts, mismatched-pin reporting, aggregation caveats, scenario identifiers and reference-case designation.
out_of_scope: The risk or opportunity entity itself: its identity, statement, status, register membership and lifecycle transitions.
The control register: control identity, design, implementation records, control ownership and control lifecycle.
Evaluation or testing of control design or operating effectiveness and the production of effectiveness determinations.
Risk treatment options, treatment plans, milestones, remediation tracking, plan-of-action records and closure.
Incidents, realized loss events, issues, near misses and post-event investigation.
Objective, asset, process and organizational-unit master data.
Setting, approving, publishing or enforcing risk appetite and tolerance thresholds.
Granting acceptance, authorization or exception decisions on a residual position.
Assessment execution, observation capture and evidence collection procedures.
Audit-trail storage, log integrity and retention execution.
Technique internals and algorithm semantics of any pinned method, including simulation, fault-tree, event-tree and Bayesian computation.
Any fixed numeric risk matrix, default likelihood band, default impact scale or universal scoring rule.
Runtime evaluation or enforcement of thresholds by a policy engine.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-015 risk / opportunity entity and lifecycle
boundary_notes.distinction: The parent model owns risk identity, statement, register status and lifecycle. This mixin attaches one assessment context to a pinned revision of that entity, carries no risk status transitions, and marks its own binding as stale when the pinned revision is superseded upstream.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Control implementation records and control assessment determinations
boundary_notes.distinction: This mixin stores control references and cites effectiveness determinations by reference; determining, testing or re-opening effectiveness belongs to the control assessment model, where assessment objectives, methods and satisfied / other-than-satisfied determinations are produced.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Risk treatment, remediation and plan-of-action records
boundary_notes.distinction: A residual estimate is an input to treatment planning. Treatment option selection, milestones, scheduling, cost tracking and closure are owned by the treatment model and are not represented here.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Assessment execution, observation and evidence records
boundary_notes.distinction: Observations and evidence are cited as the basis of an estimate. Collecting evidence, executing assessment procedures and logging assessment results are owned by the assessment-results model; this mixin holds references and a basis statement only.

The mixin references a versioned tolerance statement and records the comparison outcome. Determining appetite, approving tolerance lines and enforcing them are enterprise governance acts held elsewhere.

Accepting a residual position is an authorization act performed by a designated official and recorded in an authorization or decision model. This mixin carries only a reference to that decision and never grants, derives or enforces it.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Incident, loss event and issue records
boundary_notes.distinction: A realized event is not an assessment. Loss data may be cited as an information source for an estimate, but event records, their timelines and their consequences are owned by event models.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Risk assessment technique definitions (IEC 31010 technique catalogue and comparable method registries)
boundary_notes.distinction: The mixin pins which technique and version were applied and stores the technique's declared outputs. It never restates, parameterizes or re-implements the technique's internal semantics.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Alternative subject kind: relationship (a first-class risk-to-control association)
boundary_notes.distinction: Modelling this as a relationship was tested. A relationship entry would give each risk-control link its own identity, which suits relied-on-control attribution. It fails for the rest of the required content: assessment scope, horizon, criteria pin, likelihood and consequence dimensions, uncertainty and appetite comparison are properties of an assessment context attached to a host record, and one context routinely cites many controls and many consequences. The mixin kind is retained; the residual-change attribution is the part a Dimension may legitimately reify as a separate association record without altering this field group.

findings.name: Referenced risk identity and exact revision pin
findings.description: Identifies which risk or opportunity entity this assessment context is bound to and which exact revision of its statement was assessed, so an estimate cannot silently drift when the referenced statement is later restated. The referenced entity's own status and lifecycle stay with the owning risk model; only the local binding validity state is held here.

data_elements.name: risk-reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the risk or opportunity entity in its owning model.

data_elements.name: risk-revision-pin
data_elements.description: Exact revision, version token or immutable snapshot identifier of the assessed risk statement.

data_elements.name: risk-statement-digest
data_elements.description: Content digest of the assessed statement, allowing detection of upstream change without re-reading the source.

data_elements.name: binding-validity-state
data_elements.description: Local state of the binding: current, superseded-upstream, dangling or withdrawn. Describes this record only, never the referenced risk's own status.

data_elements.name: effect-polarity
data_elements.description: Whether the assessed effect is treated as downside, upside or two-sided under the pinned criteria.

findings.name: Objective, asset, process and context anchors
findings.description: Records what the risk is assessed against - objectives, assets, processes, organizational units, fixed contextual conditions and applicable jurisdiction or site - as references, so the estimate is interpretable and comparable only within its declared anchor set. Master data for each anchor belongs to its own registry.

data_elements.name: assessment-anchor-set
data_elements.description: The complete set of resolvable anchors this assessment is scoped against; at least one anchor must resolve for the context to be valid.

data_elements.name: objective-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an objective whose achievement the assessed uncertainty affects.

data_elements.name: asset-or-process-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an asset, process, system or service inside the assessed exposure.

data_elements.name: context-condition-statement
data_elements.description: A contextual condition held fixed for this assessment, whose change invalidates the estimate.

data_elements.name: applicable-jurisdiction-or-site
data_elements.description: Jurisdiction, site or facility whose rules or conditions make the anchor set location-specific.

findings.name: Risk source, event and consequence anchors
findings.description: Carries references to the risk source or threat source, the single event or event class whose likelihood is quantified, and the consequences included in the impact estimate, together with named exclusions. This makes likelihood and impact attach to a stated causal chain rather than to a bare label.

data_elements.name: risk-source-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the risk source or threat source the event is attributed to.

data_elements.name: event-reference-or-statement
data_elements.description: Reference to, or statement of, the event or event class whose likelihood is quantified.

data_elements.name: consequence-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a consequence included in the impact estimate.

data_elements.name: excluded-consequence-statement
data_elements.description: A consequence deliberately outside the impact estimate, recorded so the omission is visible rather than inferred.

data_elements.name: predisposing-condition-statement
data_elements.description: Vulnerability, weakness or predisposing condition assumed present for the event to occur.

data_elements.name: threat-catalogue-identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a cited external threat or hazard catalogue entry, with its naming system and version.

findings.name: Category assignment with taxonomy and version pin
findings.description: Pins the category values used to classify the referenced risk within this assessment context, together with the taxonomy scheme identifier and version, because category labels are only comparable inside one pinned scheme and category lists differ materially between frameworks.

data_elements.name: taxonomy-system-identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier or namespace of the category scheme supplying the asserted values.

data_elements.name: taxonomy-version
data_elements.description: Immutable version token of the category scheme in force for this assessment context.

data_elements.name: category-value
data_elements.description: A category value asserted against the pinned scheme.

data_elements.name: category-mapping-note
data_elements.description: Reference to a crosswalk plus the fidelity of the mapping when values are restated in another scheme.

findings.name: Assessment scope, horizon and time structure
findings.description: Declares what the assessment covers and for how long: the assessment boundary and its exclusions, the time horizon over which likelihood is expressed, the as-of time of the assessed state, the time the estimate was recorded, the validity or review-due time, and the decision the assessment was produced for.

data_elements.name: assessment-scope-statement
data_elements.description: Declared boundary of what this assessment covers.

data_elements.name: scope-exclusion-statement
data_elements.description: An element deliberately outside the assessment boundary, with the reason for exclusion.

data_elements.name: likelihood-time-horizon
data_elements.description: Period over which the likelihood or frequency dimension is expressed.

data_elements.name: assessment-as-of-time
data_elements.description: Time of the assessed state that the estimate describes, recorded in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z.

data_elements.name: assessment-recorded-time
data_elements.description: Time the estimate was produced and stored, held separately from the as-of time.

data_elements.name: validity-or-review-due-time
data_elements.description: Time after which the assessment is treated as no longer current absent revalidation.

data_elements.name: assessment-purpose
data_elements.description: The decision or reporting purpose the assessment was produced to serve.

findings.name: Criteria, method and expression-mode pin
findings.description: Pins the risk criteria set, the assessment method or technique and their versions, plus the expression mode under which values are recorded, so that a level of risk stays interpretable and so that comparison can be refused when pins differ. The mixin references method definitions and never restates technique semantics.

data_elements.name: criteria-set-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned criteria set defining scales and thresholds for this context.

data_elements.name: criteria-set-version
data_elements.description: Immutable version token of the criteria set in force.

data_elements.name: method-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assessment method or technique applied.

data_elements.name: method-version
data_elements.description: Version or edition of the applied method or technique.

data_elements.name: expression-mode
data_elements.description: How values are expressed: qualitative, ordinal, semi-quantitative, quantitative, probabilistic or scenario-based.

data_elements.name: method-definition-locator
data_elements.description: Resolvable locator of the normative definition of the pinned technique, held by its publisher.

findings.name: Likelihood and frequency expression
findings.description: Declares how the likelihood side is expressed - ordinal band, probability, frequency per unit time, qualitative descriptor or distribution - with its unit, scale reference, horizon dependency and the operations its scale type forbids.

data_elements.name: likelihood-expression-mode
data_elements.description: Form in which the likelihood side is expressed for this record.

data_elements.name: likelihood-ordinal-band
data_elements.description: Scale-referenced ordinal band value, stored as a code so that arithmetic is not implied by the encoding.

data_elements.name: likelihood-quantitative-value
data_elements.description: Probability or frequency value with its unit, where a quantitative or probabilistic mode is pinned.

data_elements.name: likelihood-scale-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the scale definition in the pinned criteria set that gives the value meaning.

data_elements.name: likelihood-decomposition
data_elements.description: Separate storage of likelihood of occurrence and likelihood of adverse impact where the pinned method distinguishes them.

data_elements.name: likelihood-distribution-parameters
data_elements.description: Parameters and bounds of a distribution or range representation of likelihood.

findings.name: Impact and consequence dimensions
findings.description: Declares the impact side, which may be multi-dimensional across financial, safety, health, fundamental-rights, environmental, operational, reputational and regulatory effects, each with its own scale, and states how or whether dimensions are combined and which parties bear each consequence.

data_elements.name: impact-dimension-set
data_elements.description: The set of impact dimensions scored in this assessment context.

data_elements.name: impact-value-per-dimension
data_elements.description: Value recorded for one impact dimension together with its scale reference and unit.

data_elements.name: impact-combination-rule
data_elements.description: Declared rule for combining dimensions, or an explicit statement that no combined value is asserted.

data_elements.name: affected-party-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a party bearing a recorded consequence, including external and vulnerable groups where relevant.

data_elements.name: consequence-order
data_elements.description: Whether a recorded consequence is primary or secondary or downstream under the pinned method.

findings.name: Inherent estimate and its exclusion statement
findings.description: Records the estimate produced before, or excluding, the effect of the referenced controls, together with an explicit statement of what inherent was taken to mean, because the term is not uniformly defined and some authorities do not require it at all. Omission must be recorded with a ground rather than left implicit.

data_elements.name: inherent-definition-statement
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of what inherent meant in this context, including which control effects were excluded.

data_elements.name: inherent-estimate-value
data_elements.description: The inherent estimate expressed under the pinned criteria, dimension by dimension.

data_elements.name: inherent-estimate-state
data_elements.description: Whether an inherent estimate is present, is an initial characterization, or was deliberately not produced.

data_elements.name: inherent-omission-ground
data_elements.description: Documented ground for omitting an inherent estimate where none was produced.

data_elements.name: inherent-derivation-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the derivation record supporting the inherent value.

findings.name: Assumptions, data basis and uncertainty qualification
findings.description: Captures the assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind and analysis constraints behind the estimate, together with confidence or data-quality grading, uncertainty representation, unmeasurable aspects and precision caveats. This is what allows a reader to judge whether a value rests on incident history, expert judgement, modelled data or a vendor claim, and how far it may be trusted.

data_elements.name: assumption-statement
data_elements.description: An explicit assumption whose falsification would change or invalidate the estimate.

data_elements.name: critical-assumption-flag
data_elements.description: Marks the assumption whose falsification would most change the recorded result.

data_elements.name: information-source-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a dataset, observation set, report or elicitation used as an input.

data_elements.name: data-currency-time
data_elements.description: Currency time of an information source, recorded separately from the assessment as-of and recording times.

data_elements.name: estimation-basis-kind
data_elements.description: Whether the estimate is judgement-elicited, data-derived, model-produced or a declared hybrid.

data_elements.name: analysis-constraint-statement
data_elements.description: A constraint on the analysis such as limited time, access or data availability.

data_elements.name: confidence-grade
data_elements.description: Confidence or data-quality grade with its scale reference.

data_elements.name: uncertainty-representation
data_elements.description: How uncertainty is expressed: range, interval, distribution, narrative caveat or none stated.

data_elements.name: unmeasurable-aspect-statement
data_elements.description: Aspect of the risk acknowledged as emergent, inscrutable or not measurable to the implied precision.

data_elements.name: precision-caveat
data_elements.description: Statement limiting the precision downstream consumers may infer from the stored notation.

findings.name: Residual estimate, control linkage and change explanation
findings.description: Records the estimate after the referenced controls are taken into account, the control references relied on, the effectiveness determinations cited for each of them, which dimension changed, and why. Effectiveness is cited by reference and is produced by the control assessment model; this finding never derives, revises or re-opens it.

data_elements.name: residual-estimate-value
data_elements.description: The residual estimate expressed under the same pinned criteria and dimensions as the inherent estimate.

data_elements.name: relied-on-control-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a control relied on when producing the residual estimate, resolving into the control implementation model.

data_elements.name: cited-effectiveness-determination-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an effectiveness determination produced by the control assessment model and cited here without restatement.

data_elements.name: reliance-without-determination-flag
data_elements.description: Marks reliance on a control for which no current effectiveness determination is available.

data_elements.name: changed-dimension
data_elements.description: Which dimension the control effect changed: likelihood, consequence or both.

data_elements.name: residual-change-explanation
data_elements.description: Narrative explanation of what changed between the inherent and residual estimates and why.

data_elements.name: estimate-characterization-state
data_elements.description: Whether this characterization is initial as first identified or adjusted after control effects were taken into account.

findings.name: Appetite or tolerance reference and comparison outcome
findings.description: References the appetite or tolerance statement in force, records the outcome of comparing the residual estimate against it, and stamps who recorded the comparison and which acceptance or authorization decision, if any, was taken elsewhere. Setting, approving and enforcing appetite are not performed here.

data_elements.name: appetite-or-tolerance-statement-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the appetite or tolerance statement in force for this comparison.

data_elements.name: appetite-statement-version
data_elements.description: Version token of the referenced appetite or tolerance statement.

data_elements.name: tolerance-threshold-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the specific threshold or tolerance line applied to a dimension.

data_elements.name: comparison-outcome
data_elements.description: Recorded outcome of comparing the residual estimate with the referenced tolerance, including a no-applicable-tolerance value.

data_elements.name: comparison-recorded-by
data_elements.description: Reference to the role or actor that recorded the comparison outcome.

data_elements.name: acceptance-decision-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an acceptance, authorization or exception decision recorded in the model that owns such decisions.

findings.name: Comparability verdicts, aggregation caveats and scenario dependence
findings.description: Records whether records may be placed on a common scale, which pins failed to match when they may not, which caveats must travel with any permitted aggregate, and how scenario variants and a designated reference case are represented. The model refuses to define a normalization algorithm it has no authority to assert.

data_elements.name: comparability-verdict
data_elements.description: Whether the compared records are comparable, comparable with caveats, or not comparable.

data_elements.name: mismatched-pin-list
data_elements.description: The specific pins that failed to match, naming criteria set, method, expression mode, scope, horizon or taxonomy.

data_elements.name: aggregation-caveat
data_elements.description: A caveat that must accompany any aggregate or roll-up built from this record.

data_elements.name: scenario-identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of a scenario under which this estimate was produced.

data_elements.name: scenario-definition-reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned scenario definition owned by the scenario or method registry.

data_elements.name: reference-case-flag
data_elements.description: Marks the scenario variant designated as the reference case for reporting.

data_elements.name: superseded-criteria-handling
data_elements.description: How a record pinned to a withdrawn criteria version is treated in a current roll-up.

findings.name: Authoritative control reference and revision binding
findings.description: Binds this assertion set to exactly one control definition in an external catalogue, pinned to a named catalogue source and revision, with the parameter values selected and any tailoring declared for the host subject. Catalogue text, families, enhancements and parameter definitions remain owned by the catalogue model.

data_elements.name: Control reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the authoritative control definition, carried in the issuing catalogue's namespace.

data_elements.name: Catalogue source reference
data_elements.description: Identifier or URI of the catalogue, profile or baseline from which the control reference is drawn.

data_elements.name: Catalogue revision pin
data_elements.description: Release, revision or version label of the catalogue in force at binding time.

data_elements.name: Selected parameter values
data_elements.description: Parameter identifier and value pairs chosen for this subject, mirroring catalogue parameter definitions without redefining them.

data_elements.name: Binding observation time
data_elements.description: Time at which the binding was captured into this model, distinct from any catalogue publication date.

findings.name: Control objective and classification projection
findings.description: The objective the control is claimed to achieve for the host subject plus classification facets: functional type (preventive, detective, corrective), execution mode (manual, automated, hybrid), operating level (entity or process/transaction) and key designation. Values are source-qualified; where a catalogue publishes its own attribute values they are carried unchanged.

data_elements.name: Subject control objective
data_elements.description: Locally authored statement of what the control is claimed to achieve for this subject.

data_elements.name: Functional type
data_elements.description: Preventive, detective or corrective classification; multi-valued where a control acts in more than one mode.

data_elements.name: Execution mode
data_elements.description: Manual, automated or hybrid execution of the control.

data_elements.name: Operating level
data_elements.description: Entity-level or process/transaction-level operation of the control.

data_elements.name: Key control designation
data_elements.description: Whether the control is designated key for the subject, with the determining party recorded in provenance.

data_elements.name: Classification vocabulary reference
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the controlled vocabulary each classification value is drawn from.

findings.name: Applicability, covered population and exclusion determination
findings.description: Declares whether the control applies to the host subject, the population or boundary it covers, the basis for that determination, and any not-applicable or partially applicable determination with justification, approval and validity window.

data_elements.name: Applicability status
data_elements.description: Applicable, partially applicable or not applicable determination for the subject.

data_elements.name: Applicability basis
data_elements.description: Documented reason the control applies, including scoping rule or obligation reference.

data_elements.name: Covered population reference
data_elements.description: References to the components, records or process instances the control is claimed to cover.

data_elements.name: Exclusion justification
data_elements.description: Justification recorded when applicability is denied or narrowed, with approver in provenance.

data_elements.name: Applicability effective-from
data_elements.description: Event time from which the applicability determination holds, distinct from the time it was recorded.

findings.name: Owner, operator, assessor and approver references
findings.description: Role-scoped references to the parties accountable for the control and its assertions, including shared, provided and inherited responsibility splits, competence and authority assertions for the performer, and independence flags for the assessor and approver. Party master data stays in the directory model.

data_elements.name: Control owner reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the accountable owner party or organisational unit.

data_elements.name: Control operator reference
data_elements.description: References to the parties or systems that perform the control.

data_elements.name: Assessor reference
data_elements.description: References to the parties that assess the control, with independence recorded separately.

data_elements.name: Responsibility split
data_elements.description: Structured allocation of provided, inherited and customer responsibility across parties.

data_elements.name: Assessor independence flag
data_elements.description: Whether the assessing or approving party is independent of the party operating the control.

findings.name: Risk-to-control link and claimed treatment mechanism
findings.description: One directed link from a risk statement reference to a control reference, carrying the claimed treatment mechanism, the risk-response type it serves, any claimed magnitude of reduction, the basis of the claim and its provenance. The risk record and its own lifecycle stay in the risk model.

data_elements.name: Risk statement reference
data_elements.description: Resolvable reference to the risk record in the owning risk register.

data_elements.name: Claimed treatment mechanism
data_elements.description: How the control is claimed to act on the risk: reduce likelihood, reduce impact, shorten detection or containment time, or support transfer.

data_elements.name: Risk response type served
data_elements.description: The risk response the link serves, drawn from the risk model's response vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Claim basis
data_elements.description: Whether the treatment claim is estimated, analytically derived or demonstrated by testing.

data_elements.name: Link assertion event time
data_elements.description: Event time at which the linkage was asserted, recorded separately from the ingestion time of the record.

findings.name: Many-to-many coverage and control dependency structure
findings.description: The aggregate view over links: which control sets cover which risks and vice versa, coverage completeness and precision, uncovered risks and unlinked controls, plus dependency and reliance edges between controls including reliance on general IT controls, shared services and inherited controls.

data_elements.name: Coverage edge set
data_elements.description: The set of risk-to-control edges scoped to the host subject, each carrying a sufficiency flag.

data_elements.name: Coverage completeness
data_elements.description: Assessed completeness of the control set against the linked risk, on a declared vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Coverage precision note
data_elements.description: Statement of the level of precision at which the control set acts relative to the risk.

data_elements.name: Control dependency reference
data_elements.description: References to controls, shared services or inherited controls this control relies on, with dependency type.

data_elements.name: Uncovered risk reference
data_elements.description: References to in-scope risks with no linked control in an operating state.

findings.name: Framework crosswalk without conformance claim
findings.description: Mappings from the bound control to entries in other frameworks, each carrying relation strength, the target framework version, the mapping author and date, and an explicit disclaimer that the mapping asserts alignment only and never conformance, implementation or effectiveness.

data_elements.name: Crosswalk target reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an entry in another catalogue or outcome framework.

data_elements.name: Crosswalk relation strength
data_elements.description: Declared relation between the bound control and the target entry.

data_elements.name: Crosswalk target version
data_elements.description: Version label of the target framework the mapping was authored against.

data_elements.name: Non-conformance disclaimer
data_elements.description: Mandatory flag asserting that the mapping establishes alignment only and confers no conformance or effectiveness meaning.

findings.name: Design adequacy assertion
findings.description: The assertion that the control, if operated as prescribed, would achieve its objective: design status, design rationale, the threshold or precision at which it would act, the determining party and time, and any recorded design limitation or design deficiency reference. Explicitly independent of whether the control is implemented or operating.

data_elements.name: Design status
data_elements.description: Assertion of design adequacy on a declared vocabulary, independent of implementation and operation.

data_elements.name: Design rationale
data_elements.description: Locally authored reasoning for the design determination, referencing but not reproducing the procedure or configuration.

data_elements.name: Design precision or threshold
data_elements.description: The threshold, tolerance or precision at which the control is designed to act.

data_elements.name: Design determination event time
data_elements.description: Event time of the design determination, recorded separately from ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Design deficiency reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a record in the deficiency and remediation model describing a design shortfall.

findings.name: Implementation state, deviations, exceptions and compensating controls
findings.description: Whether the designed control is actually in place for the subject: implementation status and scope of partial implementation, recorded deviations from the design, approved exceptions or waivers with expiry, and references to compensating or alternative controls together with the documented constraint that justifies them. Compensating control definitions and remediation workflow stay in their owning models.

data_elements.name: Implementation status
data_elements.description: Status such as implemented, partial, planned, alternative implementation or not applicable, drawn from a declared vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Deviation record
data_elements.description: Recorded departures from the designed implementation, each with a reason and approval reference.

data_elements.name: Exception or waiver reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an approved exception permitting non-implementation, held in the governance model.

data_elements.name: Exception expiry
data_elements.description: Time at which the approved exception lapses and the gap reverts to unmitigated.

data_elements.name: Compensating control reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the compensating or alternative control relied on, with an explicit sense code.

data_elements.name: Documented constraint
data_elements.description: The technical or business constraint that justifies a compensating or alternative approach.

findings.name: Operating status, frequency and triggers
findings.description: How the control actually runs: operating status kept distinct from implementation status, declared frequency or event triggers, the expected occurrence population for a stated period, observed occurrence counts obtained by reference, and suspension or dormancy handling. Execution records belong to the executing system.

data_elements.name: Operating status
data_elements.description: Whether the control is operating, suspended or not operating, distinct from implementation status.

data_elements.name: Operating frequency
data_elements.description: Declared cadence at which the control is expected to operate.

data_elements.name: Operating trigger
data_elements.description: Events that cause the control to operate where it is not periodic.

data_elements.name: Expected occurrence count
data_elements.description: Population of expected control occurrences in the stated period.

data_elements.name: Observed occurrence count
data_elements.description: Count of occurrences obtained by reference from the executing system, with its retrieval time.

data_elements.name: Operating period
data_elements.description: Start and end of the period over which operation is claimed, both RFC 3339 with offset.

findings.name: Assessment method, timing and evidence binding
findings.description: Binds an effectiveness assertion to the assessment activity and its evidence: assessment method (examine, interview, test), depth and coverage attributes, sample or population basis, assessment event time and the operating period covered, assessor reference, and evidence references with integrity digests, collection times and expiry. Test cases, results and evidence payloads remain in their owning models.

data_elements.name: Assessment reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assessment plan, activity or result record in the owning assessment model.

data_elements.name: Assessment method
data_elements.description: One or more of examine, interview and test, as defined by the assessment vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Depth and coverage attributes
data_elements.description: Rigour and breadth attributes attached to the applied assessment methods.

data_elements.name: Sample basis
data_elements.description: Population, sample size and selection method used for the assessment.

data_elements.name: Assessment event time
data_elements.description: Event time at which the assessment was performed, distinct from the binding's ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an evidence object held by the evidence model.

data_elements.name: Evidence integrity digest
data_elements.description: Digest asserted by the owning evidence model at binding time, with algorithm identifier.

findings.name: Tested effectiveness conclusion, confidence and validity
findings.description: The conclusion about operating effectiveness on a named vocabulary, with its scope, the assessment and evidence bindings that are its only permitted basis, an attached confidence and its limits, a validity window with invalidation triggers, and any deficiency severity with a reference to the record tracking remediation.

data_elements.name: Effectiveness conclusion
data_elements.description: Conclusion value on a named vocabulary, never derived from documentation, mapping or incident absence.

data_elements.name: Conclusion vocabulary
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the vocabulary the conclusion value is drawn from.

data_elements.name: Conclusion basis reference
data_elements.description: References to the assessment and evidence binding manifests that support the conclusion.

data_elements.name: Conclusion confidence
data_elements.description: Declared confidence in the conclusion together with the factors limiting it.

data_elements.name: Conclusion validity expiry
data_elements.description: Time after which the conclusion is no longer current and degrades to unknown.

data_elements.name: Deficiency severity
data_elements.description: Severity value recorded for an adverse conclusion, on the declared severity vocabulary.

findings.name: Residual contribution and acceptance linkage
findings.description: How the assessed effectiveness of this control contributes to the residual position of the linked risk: the attributed change from inherent to residual, the attribution method and its effective time, the attribution status, and references to the residual risk record and any acceptance decision. Residual values, appetite thresholds and acceptance decisions are owned by the risk model.

data_elements.name: Residual risk record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the residual risk record in the owning risk model that this contribution feeds.

data_elements.name: Attributed reduction
data_elements.description: Quantified or ordinal change from inherent to residual attributed to this control.

data_elements.name: Attribution method
data_elements.description: Method used to derive the attributed change, drawn from a declared vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Attribution status
data_elements.description: Whether the attribution is claimed, accepted by the risk owner, suspended on expiry or rejected.

data_elements.name: Attribution effective time
data_elements.description: Event time from which the attribution applies, recorded separately from ingestion time.

data_elements.name: Acceptance decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the risk acceptance or authorization decision recorded in the risk model.

findings.name: Accountable owner of the projected risk and of each linked control
findings.description: Identifies the party accountable for the residual risk conclusion on this host and the party accountable for each linked control, distinguishes accountability from delegated operational execution, and places each party in a governance line.

data_elements.name: Risk owner reference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to the party accountable for the residual risk conclusion on this host record.

data_elements.name: Control owner reference
data_elements.description: Typed reference to the party accountable for each control linked to the projected risk.

data_elements.name: Delegation reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the instrument delegating operational execution without transferring accountability.

data_elements.name: Governance line code
data_elements.description: Code placing a named party in a governing-body, first-line, second-line or independent-assurance role for this binding.

data_elements.name: Owner effective from
data_elements.description: Instant from which the recorded accountability assignment applies to this binding.

findings.name: Authority to assert, change, accept or retire a binding
findings.description: Separates authority to assert a control linkage from authority to accept the residual risk that remains, ties each act to a versioned authority threshold table, and defines admissibility preconditions for changing an already accepted binding.

data_elements.name: Required authority level
data_elements.description: Authority level that the acting party had to hold for the recorded act on this binding.

data_elements.name: Risk acceptance decision reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authoritative decision accepting the residual risk for this host record.

data_elements.name: Authority basis reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the policy, charter or delegation that confers the authority exercised.

data_elements.name: Authority threshold table version
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the table mapping residual severity bands to required authority levels.

data_elements.name: Authorization time
data_elements.description: Instant at which the authorising act occurred, recorded separately from the instant it was ingested into this model.

findings.name: Segregation of duties and reviewer independence
findings.description: Declares which combinations of asserting, reviewing, approving and accepting the same binding are incompatible for one actor, what establishes reviewer independence from control design and operation, and how overrides and after-the-fact breaches are handled.

data_elements.name: Incompatible duty pair
data_elements.description: Declared pair of acts on the same binding that one actor may not perform.

data_elements.name: Reviewer independence basis
data_elements.description: Code stating the basis on which the reviewer is independent of control design and operation, with identified threats and safeguards.

data_elements.name: Duty-separation override reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a time-bounded, authorised override of a declared incompatible duty pair.

findings.name: Assessment criteria binding and conflict resolution
findings.description: Records which versioned criteria, scale and risk-appetite statement produced the residual conclusion, what makes those criteria suitable, and which verdict prevails when two applicable frameworks disagree on the same binding.

data_elements.name: Criteria reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the versioned risk and effectiveness criteria applied to this binding.

data_elements.name: Scale version
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the severity, likelihood or effectiveness scale used.

data_elements.name: Risk appetite reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the appetite or acceptance threshold statement against which residual risk was judged acceptable.

data_elements.name: Prevailing framework code
data_elements.description: Code naming the framework whose verdict governs where applicable criteria conflict.

data_elements.name: Conflict resolution basis
data_elements.description: Recorded rationale and precedence rule applied when criteria produced divergent verdicts.

findings.name: Assurance level, scope limitations and inherited reliance
findings.description: Records the level of assurance a control effectiveness conclusion carries, the methods and objects actually examined, what was excluded from scope, and the carve-outs limiting reliance on third-party reports.

data_elements.name: Assurance level
data_elements.description: Declared level of assurance carried by the effectiveness conclusion, distinguishing reasonable from limited assurance and unassured self-assertion.

data_elements.name: Assessment method
data_elements.description: Method applied to reach the conclusion, such as examine, interview or test, with the objects to which it was applied.

data_elements.name: Scope exclusion
data_elements.description: Statement of a population, period or environment segment excluded from the assessment.

data_elements.name: Inherited assurance report reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an external assurance or attestation report relied upon for this conclusion.

data_elements.name: Assessment coverage period
data_elements.description: Start and end of the period the conclusion covers, distinct from the instant the conclusion was reached.

findings.name: Host-scoped lifecycle state of the binding
findings.description: Enumerates the states a risk-control binding may occupy on its host record, the permitted transitions, the constraint the host lifecycle imposes, and how duplicate active bindings between the same risk and control are resolved.

data_elements.name: Binding state
data_elements.description: Current host-scoped state of the binding, such as draft, asserted, under review, accepted, expired, superseded, withdrawn or tombstoned.

data_elements.name: State entered at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the binding entered its current state.

data_elements.name: Transition reason
data_elements.description: Code explaining why the binding moved to its current state.

data_elements.name: Host record reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the record onto which this risk-control binding is projected.

findings.name: Assessment currency, expiry and reassessment triggers
findings.description: Defines how long a residual risk and effectiveness conclusion remains valid, which events force reassessment ahead of schedule, what status an expired but unreassessed binding carries, and which timestamp starts the currency clock.

data_elements.name: Assessed at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the assessor reached the recorded conclusion, distinct from the instant the conclusion was ingested.

data_elements.name: Valid until
data_elements.description: Instant after which the recorded conclusion is no longer current absent reassessment.

data_elements.name: Review interval
data_elements.description: Maximum interval between systematic reviews of this binding.

data_elements.name: Currency status
data_elements.description: Derived status expressing whether the conclusion is current, approaching expiry, expired or invalidated.

data_elements.name: Reassessment trigger
data_elements.description: Code identifying an event that obliges reassessment before scheduled expiry, such as a host change, control failure, post-market signal or criteria change.

findings.name: Revision, supersession and correction of relied-upon assertions
findings.description: Determines whether a corrected assertion keeps its identifier with a new revision or receives a successor identifier, what a supersession record must state, which fields may never be edited in place, and who must be notified downstream.

data_elements.name: Revision identifier
data_elements.description: Monotonic identifier of this revision of the binding, used for optimistic concurrency and for citing a specific state of the record.

data_elements.name: Supersedes reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assertion revision that this revision replaces.

data_elements.name: Superseded by reference
data_elements.description: Back-reference from a superseded assertion to its successor.

data_elements.name: Correction reason
data_elements.description: Code classifying the defect that made supersession necessary, such as factual error, criteria change, scope error or evidence withdrawal.

data_elements.name: Reliance period
data_elements.description: Period during which the superseded assertion was published and could have been relied upon.

findings.name: Provenance and attribution of the assertion
findings.description: Records which agent asserted the binding, on whose behalf it acted, which assessment activity generated the conclusion, what it was derived from, and whether the assertion is human-attested or machine-generated.

data_elements.name: Asserting agent reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the agent that asserted this binding revision.

data_elements.name: Acted on behalf of reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the party on whose behalf the asserting agent acted.

data_elements.name: Assertion activity reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the assessment or review activity that generated the conclusion.

data_elements.name: Derived from reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a prior assertion, external report or dataset from which this conclusion was derived.

data_elements.name: Agent kind
data_elements.description: Code distinguishing a human, organisational or software agent as the author of the assertion.

data_elements.name: Recorded at
data_elements.description: Instant at which this model ingested the assertion, held separately from the instant the assessed condition or decision occurred.

findings.name: Evidence reference integrity and immutability
findings.description: Binds each item of supporting evidence to the assertion so that later substitution is detectable, fixes which attributes become immutable at approval, and defines the treatment of evidence that becomes unavailable or is lawfully destroyed.

data_elements.name: Evidence reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an evidence object supporting the assertion; required from the reviewed state onward.

data_elements.name: Evidence digest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest of the referenced evidence object as observed at assertion time.

data_elements.name: Digest algorithm
data_elements.description: Identifier of the algorithm used to compute the evidence digest.

data_elements.name: Evidence observed at
data_elements.description: Instant at which the evidence object was observed and its digest computed.

data_elements.name: Evidence availability status
data_elements.description: Code stating whether referenced evidence remains retrievable, is withheld, is disposed of, or fails digest verification.

findings.name: Sensitivity labelling and disclosure-profiled export
findings.description: Assigns handling labels to the binding and its parts, defines which fields are withheld, generalised or hashed for each audience, identifies personal data, and governs authorisation of out-of-profile release and re-identification checks.

data_elements.name: Sensitivity label
data_elements.description: Handling label governing onward sharing of the binding or one of its elements, drawn from a versioned label vocabulary.

data_elements.name: Field disclosure rule
data_elements.description: Rule stating, per field, whether it is released, withheld, generalised or hashed for a given disclosure profile.

data_elements.name: Audience reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the audience or recipient community entitled to a disclosure profile.

data_elements.name: Personal data indicator
data_elements.description: Indicates whether the binding contains data relating to identified or identifiable individuals.

data_elements.name: Release authorization reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the authorisation permitting a release outside the audience's normal disclosure profile.

findings.name: Regional and sector profiles, exceptions and external mappings
findings.description: Declares which regional or sector profile is in force over what period, which profile requirements are formally excepted and on what compensating condition, how profile conflicts are resolved, and how the binding maps to external assessment exchange schemas.

data_elements.name: Profile reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a regional or sector profile constraining this binding.

data_elements.name: Profile effective period
data_elements.description: Period over which the referenced profile applies to this binding.

data_elements.name: External schema mapping
data_elements.description: Mapping from this mixin's fields to an external assessment or risk exchange schema, with its version.

data_elements.name: Unmapped field
data_elements.description: Field with no equivalent in the target exchange schema, recorded to make export lossiness explicit.

data_elements.name: Profile exception reference
data_elements.description: Reference to a granted, time-bounded exception from a profile requirement.

findings.name: Retention, legal hold and tombstone semantics
findings.description: Records which retention schedule and disposition authority govern the binding, when the retention clock starts, how a hold suspends the normal disposition cycle, what survives in a tombstone, and which external owner actually executes destruction.

data_elements.name: Retention schedule reference
data_elements.description: Reference to the approved schedule and disposition authority governing this binding's records.

data_elements.name: Retention clock start
data_elements.description: Instant from which the retention period is counted, such as the binding reaching a terminal state or the host being withdrawn from service.

data_elements.name: Legal hold reference
data_elements.description: Reference to an active hold or freeze suspending the normal disposition cycle for this binding and its evidence manifest.

data_elements.name: Disposition status
data_elements.description: Code stating whether the record is retained, eligible for disposition, held, disposition requested, or disposed of.

data_elements.name: Tombstone identifier
data_elements.description: Identifier of the surviving marker left after disposition of the substantive record.

functions.name: Bind an assessment context to a referenced risk
functions.description: Creates a revision-pinned binding between one host record and one referenced risk, capturing anchors, taxonomy pin, scope, horizon and criteria/method pins. It establishes context only and never creates, alters or advances the referenced risk entity.

functions.name: Record an estimate under a pinned method
functions.description: Stores an estimate in either the inherent or residual role exactly as produced by the pinned method, together with its dimensions, units, scale references and expression mode. It performs no method-specific computation and invents no scale semantics.

functions.name: Compare inherent and residual estimates
functions.description: Records the difference between an inherent and a residual estimate, the dimensions that changed, the controls relied on and the effectiveness determinations cited, and the outcome of comparing the residual position with a referenced tolerance statement.

functions.name: Explain assumptions and evidential basis
functions.description: Assembles and records the assumptions, information sources, data currency, estimation basis kind, analysis constraints and uncertainty qualification behind an estimate, and emits the basis statement and derivation record artifacts.

functions.name: Check comparability before comparison, reuse or aggregation
functions.description: Compares the pin sets of two or more assessment-context records against a requested comparison or aggregation operation and returns a verdict, the mismatched pins and the caveat set that any permitted result must carry.

functions.name: Link risk to control
functions.description: Create a directed risk-to-control link carrying the claimed treatment mechanism, the risk response type it serves and the basis of the claim.

functions.name: Retire risk-to-control link
functions.description: Retire or supersede an existing link without destroying it, recording the reason and any replacement link.

functions.name: Record control applicability
functions.description: Record or revise an applicability, partial-applicability or not-applicable determination for a control against the host subject, with basis, covered population and approval.

functions.name: Record design, implementation and operating assertion
functions.description: Record or revise the three state assertions for a control and subject, each with its own basis, determining party and event time, including deviations, exceptions and compensating control references.

functions.name: Bind assessment and evidence references
functions.description: Bind assessment references, applied methods, depth, coverage, sample basis, timing and assessor to a control assertion, together with evidence references and their integrity digests.

functions.name: Record effectiveness conclusion
functions.description: Record an effectiveness conclusion with its vocabulary, scope, basis references, confidence, validity window, invalidation triggers and any deficiency severity.

functions.name: Explain residual contribution
functions.description: Produce a traceable explanation of how a control's assessed effectiveness contributes to the residual position of a linked risk, and submit the attribution to the risk model.

functions.name: Authorize a binding change
functions.description: Determines whether a proposed create, link, unlink, update, accept or retire action on a WM-XCT-027 binding is admissible, by checking the acting party's authority level against the versioned threshold table and the declared incompatible-duty set. This decides admissibility for this model's own records only; runtime policy evaluation and enforcement remain with the referenced authorization model.

functions.name: Review and approve or reject an assertion
functions.description: Records an independent review of an asserted binding and the resulting approval, rejection or return for rework, capturing the reviewer's independence basis, the assurance level reached and any scope limitation.

functions.name: Reconcile bindings against host and referenced registries
functions.description: Checks referential integrity of every binding against its host record, the referenced risk register, the control catalogue, the party registry and the evidence store, and reports orphans, retired references, duplicate active bindings and unjustified control exclusions.

functions.name: Evaluate assessment currency and expire stale conclusions
functions.description: Derives the currency status of each binding from its assessment instant, review interval, validity window and fired reassessment triggers, and marks conclusions approaching expiry, expired or invalidated.

functions.name: Supersede or correct an assertion
functions.description: Issues a successor revision that replaces a relied-upon assertion, records the defect corrected and the reliance period, and notifies declared downstream consumers. Immutable fields are never edited in place.

functions.name: Produce a disclosure-profiled export
functions.description: Generates an export of one or more bindings under a named disclosure profile, applying field-level withholding, generalisation or hashing, carrying the sensitivity label on the output and recording the release.

functions.name: Apply or release a legal hold
functions.description: Places a binding and its evidence manifest under a hold that suspends the normal disposition cycle, or releases that hold on written instruction from the authorised party.

functions.name: Compute disposition eligibility and request disposition
functions.description: Determines whether a binding's records have reached the end of their retention period with no active hold, issues a disposition request to the owning records capability, and records the confirmed outcome as a tombstone. This function never performs destruction itself.

composition.target: WM-KNW-015 - Risk / Opportunity entity and lifecycle
composition.purpose: The parent model owns risk identity, statement, register membership, status and lifecycle transitions. This mixin attaches one assessment context to a pinned revision of that entity, carries only its own binding validity state, and reproduces no risk lifecycle or register operations.

composition.target: Host record of the adopting Dimension that carries risk-control linkage fields
composition.purpose: Defines how this field group is embedded on a host entity, event or decision record so a Dimension can carry a defensible assessment context without standing up a separate register.

composition.target: Control implementation and control assessment records (control register, implemented requirements, effectiveness determinations)
composition.purpose: Supplies control identity, implementation statements and effectiveness determinations that the residual estimate cites. Assessment procedures, objectives, methods and the production of determinations remain wholly with that model; this mixin carries only the reference and the reliance parameters specific to this assessment.

composition.target: Risk criteria and assessment-method registry (criteria sets, scales, thresholds, technique definitions)
composition.purpose: Supplies the versioned criteria scales and technique definitions that this mixin pins. The mixin stores the pin, the version token and the expression mode; it never defines, parameterizes or re-implements technique semantics.

composition.target: Risk appetite and tolerance statements

boundaryDecision.rationale: Two axes must be kept apart. On the record plane the frozen registry classifies vr.wm-xct-027 as a child record embedded under parent WM-KNW-015 rather than a standalone model plane; that classification governs registration and inheritance only and is not itself a subject-model kind. On the subject-model plane the defensible schema kind for the retained core is mixin: bundles 1-3 and 7-9 are a reusable, host-scoped field group with no independent identity, whose lifecycle is expressly host-scoped (rctl-gov-binding-state inline rationale) and whose content is reference pins, estimate slots, verdicts and governance stamps. The pack's own rejection of relationship is sound - assessment scope, horizon, criteria pin, likelihood and consequence dimensions, uncertainty and appetite comparison are properties of a context that cites many controls and many consequences, not of one edge. The status is split rather than accepted because bundles 4-6 (rctl-control-definition-binding, rctl-control-linkage-topology, rctl-control-assurance) author durable local artifacts - implementation assertion records, assessment/evidence manifests, effectiveness conclusion statements and a coverage matrix - that the same record's scope_statement, out_of_scope list, boundary note 2 and the rctl-risk-residual-estimate inline rationale all disclaim as owned elsewhere. The retained mixin keeps risk binding, framing, estimation, residual position, comparability and governance; the control design/implementation/operating/effectiveness authoring plane and the cross-record coverage matrix move to the control assessment model already named as their owner, leaving citation-by-reference behind. This split is the adjudicated boundary action to be recorded in the draft; it does not stop publication of a single reviewable draft carrying the hold.

decisions.concept: Subject-model entry kind for the retained core (mixin vs relationship vs entity)
decisions.disposition: accepted as mixin
decisions.rationale: The retained content has no identity independent of a host record, declares its lifecycle host-scoped, and stores pins, slots and verdicts rather than an authored subject. The pack's counter-test against relationship holds: one assessment context routinely cites many controls and many consequences, so an edge-identity kind cannot carry scope, horizon, criteria pin, dimensions, uncertainty or appetite comparison.

decisions.concept: Aggregate root ambiguity across the three merged passes
decisions.disposition: reclassified to one host-scoped assessment-context root
decisions.rationale: Three roots are implied at once: an assessment context (risk pass), a control assertion set bound to exactly one catalogue entry (rctl-control-catalogue-binding), and a risk-control edge (rctl-gov-binding-state). crud.create admits a binding with at least one control reference while the duplicate rule and rctl-gov-q-state-concurrent key on a single risk-control pair. The synthesizer must fix the root at the host-scoped context and restate edge cardinality as a contained collection, not a second root.

decisions.concept: Control assurance authoring plane in bundle rctl-control-assurance
decisions.disposition: split out to the control assessment model
decisions.rationale: out_of_scope excludes evaluation or testing of control design and operating effectiveness and the production of effectiveness determinations, and boundary note 2 assigns them to the control assessment model, yet rctl-control-artifact-effectiveness-conclusion-statement, rctl-control-artifact-implementation-assertion-record and rctl-control-fn-record-effectiveness-conclusion author exactly those objects locally. The record contradicts its own contract and must cite rather than author.

decisions.concept: Local coverage matrix artifact rctl-control-artifact-coverage-matrix
decisions.disposition: rejected as an authored local artifact
decisions.rationale: rctl-risk-comparability-limits declares no local aggregate artifact because aggregates belong to the enterprise reporting model, and known_omissions states aggregation semantics are not modelled. A many-to-many matrix spanning many risks, controls and hosts is cross-record state a host-scoped field group cannot own. Retain the traversal question, drop the authored matrix.

decisions.concept: Non-retrievable standards carried as tier-1 primary support
decisions.disposition: reclassified to scope-level alignment with explicit non-retrieval markers
decisions.rationale: known_omissions records that ISO/IEC 27001 and 27002 returned HTTP 403 and that ISO 31000 and the COSO texts were paywalled or unretrievable, yet SRC-030, SRC-031, SRC-013 and SRC-026 are listed primary_source true and SRC-030 and SRC-031 carry seven or more governance nodes and functions as source_refs. Support may not be asserted at a tier the pack simultaneously declares it does not hold.

decisions.concept: AI Act citation provenance, SRC-012 republication against SRC-034 official text
decisions.disposition: rejected as primary support; re-point or dual-cite to SRC-034
decisions.rationale: SRC-012 is a tier-3 third-party republication yet is load-bearing in rctl-risk-consequence-dimension, rctl-risk-residual-estimate, rctl-risk-appetite-comparison, boundary note 6 and rctl-risk-fn-compare-inherent-residual, while SRC-034 supplies the tier-1 EUR-Lex text in the same pack. The coverage gap note also says the AI Act was read via republication rather than EUR-Lex, contradicting SRC-034's own entry.

decisions.concept: Artifact identity strategies that embed version tokens
decisions.disposition: rejected as written; narrow the global rule or rewrite three strategies
decisions.rationale: identity_priority forbids a version tag as an identifier alone or in combination, but rctl-risk-criteria-pin-record combines a governed IRI with an immutable version token, rctl-gov-art-criteria-binding combines a criteria-version IRI with a binding revision IRI, and rctl-gov-art-disclosure-profile appends a semantic version. Either the global prohibition is narrowed to bare or leading version tags, or the three strategies are restated.

decisions.concept: Access scope enumeration omits the field plane
decisions.disposition: rejected as written; field scope must be declared
decisions.rationale: access.scopes lists bundle, layer, finding and artifact, which are research-structure planes, while crud.read promises a field projection and rctl-gov-q-sens-field requires field-level withholding, generalisation or hashing. The enforcement surface the model declares does not include the plane its own disclosure rules operate on.

decisions.concept: Precedence among the five declared access exceptions
decisions.disposition: deferred pending a declared precedence rule
decisions.rationale: Unfettered reviewer access, statutory unredacted release and restriction of a binding disclosing an exploitable unremediated weakness can collide on the same record with no ordering stated, even though the model does declare precedence for conflicting regional and sector profiles. The asymmetry must be closed before enforcement can be delegated coherently.

decisions.concept: Hard-delete precondition for unreviewed draft assertions
decisions.disposition: rejected as unverifiable within the declared boundary
decisions.rationale: crud.delete permits an author to hard-delete a draft provided no external consumer has read it, while access.audit_requirements state the model retains only references and does not reproduce, reconcile or assert completeness of the audit trail. The model cannot establish the precondition it conditions destruction on; the rule must be restated as a delegated check.

decisions.concept: Claimed count of fifteen composition links
decisions.disposition: rejected as unsupported by the delivered structure
decisions.rationale: The relationships checklist entry asserts fifteen composition links recording neighbour ownership, and the adversarial checks reference composition rationales, but the pack delivers only nine boundary_notes and no composition-link array. Either the links are emitted or the count is corrected; an uncorroborated count inflates the ownership evidence the split decision depends on.

decisions.concept: rctl-risk-fn-compare-inherent-residual recording a difference
decisions.disposition: reclassified to a change-set record with mode-gated arithmetic
decisions.rationale: The declared conflict on ordinal scales states the model stores scale-referenced codes and refuses implicit arithmetic, yet the function description records the difference between two estimates. A difference is undefined under qualitative, ordinal and scenario-based expression modes; the function must record changed dimensions and direction, computing a magnitude only where the pinned expression mode admits it.

decisions.concept: Coverage verdicts for retention, privacy and security dimensions
decisions.disposition: reclassified to covered-by-service-layer
decisions.rationale: Each of these dimensions is marked covered while the structured question set carries exactly one question of the corresponding kind across 176 questions, with the weight resting on crud, policies and access prose. The verdict is defensible only if it names the service layer as the carrier, otherwise it overstates finding-level coverage.

decisions.concept: Missing reconciliation report artifact
decisions.disposition: rejected as an undeclared but published output
decisions.rationale: serial_naming_rule enumerates reconciliation reports among serial artifacts and the Model steward role publishes them, and rctl-gov-fn-reconcile-bindings produces them, yet no artifact and no identity strategy is declared anywhere in the structure. A durable, published, serial output must carry an identity rule or be withdrawn from the naming rule and the role.

decisions.concept: Handling of superseded GAO-14-704G alongside GAO-25-107721
decisions.disposition: accepted
decisions.rationale: The pack cites both editions, marks the superseded one at a lower authority tier, records the supersession as a named conflict, states which edition governs on divergence, and limits use of the older text to the two passages whose full text was retrievable. This is the correct pattern and should be preserved verbatim through synthesis.

decisions.concept: Refusal to define a risk matrix, default bands or a normalization algorithm
decisions.disposition: accepted
decisions.rationale: No grid, default likelihood band, impact scale or scoring formula appears anywhere; expression mode plus a resolvable scale reference carries the semantics, prohibited operations derive from the declared scale type, and aggregation is gated by a comparability verdict with non-strippable caveats. This restraint is the strongest part of the record and must survive the split intact.

deferredResearch: Emit the composition-link set the coverage checklist claims (fifteen links) or correct the count to the nine delivered boundary notes, and bind each link to the neighbour model that owns the adjacent concept, since the split decision rests on that ownership evidence.
